data.body:
Brainstorm decision and OSS prior-art audit (2026-09-02)

User decision: rebar must not execute Terraform itself, and should reuse authoritative, actively maintained OSS projects for Terraform validation/analysis wherever possible rather than reimplementing their logic. Treat orchestration, isolation, provenance, normalization, and policy as rebar-owned; treat Terraform parsing/rules as upstream-owned.

Current prior-art findings:
- TFLint (terraform-linters/tflint, 5.8k stars, active 2026-08-29) is the closest analog. It does not invoke Terraform. It statically parses/evaluates HCL using HCL/cty plus a fork of Terraform internals, treats dynamic values as unknown, and emits JSON/SARIF. Its bundled Terraform-language rules need no downloaded plugin. It does launch ruleset subprocesses, so rebar must supply its own config and allow only the bundled ruleset; never honor repository plugin config or run tflint --init. Remote modules are not fetched by default and require prior terraform init/get plus opt-in --call-module-type=all; rebar should use --call-module-type=none or a deliberate local-only policy.
- HashiCorp terraform-config-inspect is a narrow, authoritative source parser/CLI. It explicitly processes only stable top-level module metadata to reduce synchronization burden. Good for extracting provider/module declarations, variables, outputs, and resources; not a semantic validator.
- Checkov (9k stars, active 2026-08-30) statically parses Terraform and builds a graph without invoking Terraform. External-module downloads are disabled unless requested; --framework terraform --download-external-modules false --skip-download provides a plausible offline, structured-output adapter. Its authority is security/misconfiguration policy, not Terraform acceptance.
- Trivy (37.7k stars, active 2026-09-01) corroborates the static-analysis pattern and explicitly treats data sources/computed values as unknown. However its Terraform parser allows remote-module downloads by default, and its CLI flag only excludes downloaded-module findings rather than clearly disabling downloads. It is not the safest first adapter without an egress sandbox.
- terraform-docs is not a safe generic adapter merely because it normally parses source: project/config options can cause it to run terraform output -json, and it supports executable plugins.
- terraform-ls is not static-only. It automatically invokes terraform version -json and terraform providers schema -json for recognized roots; formatting, validation, init, and other paths invoke more Terraform operations. It also makes Registry/Algolia requests. It can only be made non-executing through a pinned-version, scrubbed-environment containment contract, so it should not be the v1 authority.
- Across mature tools, static analysis is explicitly incomplete: unknown runtime/cloud values remain unknown; source findings are advisory; higher-fidelity plan analysis consumes an already-produced plan/plan JSON rather than creating one.

Design implication: replace REB-640's current terraform validate/live-terraform plan execution premise. The likely lane is (1) source/module metadata from an authoritative parser, (2) curated static diagnostics from TFLint and optionally a security scanner, and (3) optional analysis of a caller/CI-supplied plan artifact. Rebar never initializes modules/providers, executes Terraform/OpenTofu/provider binaries, or acquires cloud credentials.
